A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 36 readable pages, including Appendices A–E. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching of the text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations, supervision and mitigation experiments, OOD tests, shortcut counts, and numerical checks of Assumption 3.8 in Section 5 and Appendices B and E.2.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendices B and E.2, including benchmark scores and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The architectures, DPL* and bears* adaptations, training objectives, inference procedures, and mitigation methods are unchanged. Sparsity regularization appears in a new discussion of concurrent work, without being incorporated into this paper's methods.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST-Add, MNIST-SumParity, its biased OOD variant, Clevr, and BDD-OIA. The language-model setting mentioned in the added reference does not extend the paper's experimental coverage.

E2.justification: DPL, CBNM, SENN, DSL, DPL*, bears*, and the appendix CBNM variants retain their experiment-specific participation in Tables 1–5 and 11–14. The newly cited Goyal et al. method is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A retain the same splits, preprocessing, concept alignment, metrics, supervision settings, training budgets, and model-selection procedures. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The mitigation and supervision sweeps, OOD tests, confusion matrices, learned-layer analyses, shortcut counting, and numerical evaluation of Assumption 3.8 are unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices B and E.2.

E5.justification: Appendix A.6 retains five-seed averaging, and Figures 5–6 retain standard-deviation reporting over five seeds. The repeated-run information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All original numerical and qualitative results match, including Tables 1–5 and 11–15, the empirical figures, and Appendix E.2's extremality checks. No result entries, scores, rankings, or experimental findings are added or removed.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, Theorems 3.6 and 3.9, and mathematical material in Appendices C–E are unchanged. The new reference to Goyal et al.'s Theorem 2 summarizes another work without adding a formal statement or proof here.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about joint reasoning shortcuts, identifiability conditions, and the limited effectiveness of tested mitigations.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly interprets concurrent concept-recovery guarantees under label supervision and sparsity regularization as avoiding JRSs. This adds a concrete qualification about possible successful mitigation; interpretations of the paper's own experiments and its stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A's implementation details, hyperparameters, software versions, A100 hardware information, and code/data sourcing are unchanged. The added bibliographic URL does not change access to experimental resources.

R1.justification: v3 adds Goyal et al. (2025), Causal differentiating concepts, as reference 101 and discusses its relationship to intended semantics and JRS avoidance in Section 6. Existing cited works are retained, with subsequent references renumbered.

P1.justification: The textual revision consists of a short addition to Section 6, updated title-page dates and version information, and citation renumbering. Section ordering and the remaining prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: All 13 figures and 15 tables retain their content, design, and placement. Added prose shifts the subsequent text downward on page 10, and the new reference extends the bibliography on page 15, producing limited layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves research positioning and interpretive balance by acknowledging concurrent work and connecting its reported recovery guarantee to JRS avoidance in Section 6. The empirical evidence, proofs, and existing limitations remain unchanged, so the quality gain is limited to this substantive contextual addition.
